=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package is not acceptable as drafted. It shifts most known risks to the Buyer through general disclosure, a buyer-knowledge bar, and caps that apply to every claim type. Its "FINAL, not to be re-opened" label does not bind Wattlebridge. This is a Seller draft for mark-up, and the Buyer should negotiate it as one. The market ranges the Seller cites should be checked against the deal team's own precedents before they are used in negotiation.

Percentages below are against the AUD 24m price.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** AUD 4.8m (20% of price) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap, such as 50% (AUD 12m) as an opening position, with a fallback floor of about 30% (AUD 7.2m) if diligence is clean. Fundamental, tax, and specific indemnity claims should be capped at the full price.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's own known exposures (about AUD 4.1m across Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and Sandbar) nearly consume the cap, so the cap would protect the Seller more than the Buyer.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket (about 1.04% of price) operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A de minimis of about AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket (once exceeded, the whole claim is recoverable) of about 0.5% (AUD 120k). Specific indemnities, fundamental claims and tax claims excluded from both thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible basket. A tipping basket is the standard Buyer position and avoids the Buyer absorbing the first AUD 250k of any loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, with that limit applied to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 to 36 months for general warranties, so the Buyer can cover at least one full audit and tax cycle after FY26. Fundamental and title claims at 6 years or the statutory limitation period, whichever is longer. Tax claims to run until 60 days after the ATO's amendment period closes.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A single 18-month limit for all claims would cut off tax and title claims that typically surface later.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full price, with a separate longer time limit, and outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title failure is the most serious risk on a share sale and should not be capped like a general warranty.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not addressed. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which would reach fraud claims.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that caps, time limits, disclosure, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions do not apply to fraud, fraudulent concealment, or wilful misrepresentation.
- **Recommendation:** Insert. Without it, the Seller's limitations could be argued to cover the Seller's own dishonesty.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Schedule 7 and DD Letter §1.1–1.2 disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against specific warranties, with reasonable detail. No general data room disclosure. Disclosure should not qualify fundamental, tax or IP warranties unless specifically disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. Data room disclosure would disclose everything, including the DD-002 to DD-012 issues, without requiring any warranty to be accurate.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Delete clause 8.3. Add an express clause confirming that the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights to claim. Known issues (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar, export incident, Bluefen) should be dealt with through specific indemnities or price adjustments, not warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Combined with the 20% cap, this clause would leave the Buyer with no practical recourse for the issues it has already identified. Australian law on buyer knowledge is not settled enough to rely on by default, so the clause should be expressly addressed.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty written consent. DD-002 reports about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (about 30%). No final written consent or evidence that conditions 11.3 are met.
- **Buyer should want:** Final written Bluefen consent, and evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. A walk right if not satisfied. Specific indemnity for any loss from Bluefen terminating or renegotiating.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent. Reasonable endeavours is not enough when about 30% of revenue depends on it.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. Facility not repaid. No discharge of security included.
- **Buyer should want:** Payout at Completion from the purchase price under a payoff letter. Executed discharge of security and PPSR cancellation delivered at Completion. Any shortfall borne by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. The Buyer would otherwise take the company subject to a security interest over its assets with no release in hand, and debt-free pricing already requires debt to be settled out of the price.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses, "a matter for the Seller," not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and superannuation treatment unstated.
- **Buyer should want:** All Completion bonuses, plus associated payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, treated as debt-like items and deducted from price, or paid by the Seller at Completion. A specific indemnity for any bonus or employment claims arising before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. These are transaction-linked liabilities that a debt-free, cash-free price should not pass to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of project materials on payment of all SOW3 fees. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Evidence of payment or payment of the AUD 180k before Completion (or a price deduction). A confirmatory assignment of SOW3 project materials at Completion. A broader specific IP indemnity covering title to, and infringement risk in, the Ironquay materials, with IP warranties treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Limiting it to one payment leaves the Buyer exposed to title and third-party claims over the materials.

### SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 describes a download link sent to an unintended external address, possibly exposing about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). The investigation is preliminary. The Seller calls it "not expected to be material" and states no loss.
- **Buyer should want:** Completion of a forensic investigation before signing or Completion. A determination of whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, covering regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs. Longer survival, and possibly an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific indemnity and pre-Completion investigation. The Seller's materiality view is not a basis for the Buyer to accept the risk.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k (about AUD 110k each), described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of contract terms, term length, termination rights and whether any amounts are prepaid, accrued or payable pre-Completion. Any pre-Completion or committed liabilities treated as debt-like or adjusted in working capital.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" as a blanket characterisation. Renewals affecting the price basis need review of the actual terms.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Fundamental, tax and IP warranties folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate tiers with their own caps, time limits and thresholds: general warranties; fundamental/title; tax (with a pre-Completion tax indemnity); IP; and specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Separate categories are the standard way to match risk to the correct protection.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%. The Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** An independent ASIC company search, inspection of the original register and share certificates, a PPSR and encumbrance search, confirmation of no options or other rights over shares, and executed transfer documents as Completion deliverables. Title warranties as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification now. A seller-maintained register is not sufficient evidence of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Specific tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a claim period running to the ATO amendment period. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and open-source use, treated as fundamental or at least outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Tax and IP are high-risk areas for a SaaS business and should not be subject to general limits.

---

### Other items flagged but outside your list
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction. Confirm whether the share sale triggers a change-of-control consent. The disclosure does not say it does.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale. The disclosure only describes a notification obligation.
- **Schedule 7 and clause 1.4 of the Disclosure Letter:** Non-admission language should be reviewed alongside SPA-N-006.

### Priority actions
1. Reject the general disclosure, buyer-knowledge and "FINAL" positions in the cover letter.
2. Make Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout and title verification conditions to Completion.
3. Settle the price mechanics: bonuses, Ironquay and Riverlark as debt or debt-like items, and the Sandbar position.
4. Require specific indemnities for the Ironquay, export incident, and bonus matters.
5. Restructure the caps, time limits and thresholds into separate categories, with a fraud carve-out.

These positions are for the deal team's negotiation strategy. Market ranges, NSW limitation periods, Privacy Act obligations, and the tax amendment period should be confirmed by the responsible Australian lawyer before they go into the mark-up.
